newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Singapore Port in talks on Sri Lanka Galle port.
newsitem.headline: Singapore Port in talks on Sri Lanka Galle port.

text.p: A British-Chinese consortium planning to build a new trans-shipment port near Sri Lanka's southern Galle harbour is holding talks with the Port Authority of Singapore (PSA), a spokesman said on Wednesday.
"We're holding talks with the Singapore Port Authority on operating the new Galle port once it is built," Suppiah Kandasamy, the chairman of the consortium, told Reuters.
The PSA could come in as an equity partner in the $350 million project or manage the port on a fee basis, he said.

The consortium was also holding talks for management of the new Galle port with China's Cosco Container Lines, a Malaysian port management company and a Canadian port construction and management firm, he said.

The consortium, led by Mott Macdonald of Britain, consists of three Chinese firms coordinated by China-Lanka International, and the project has been promoted by Kandasmay's Construction and Personnel Services.
Kandasamy said the consortium has to submit to the Sri Lankan government by April 30 its proposals to raise funds for the project.
The new port near the ancient Galle harbour, which will take three years to build, will have five berths with a capacity of a million containers a year.
The consortium expects trans-shipment traffic to account for 80 percent of the volume in the new Galle port, half of which would be from the Indian sub-continent.
Galle, 115 km (70 miles) south of Colombo, is considered a better location for trans-shipment than Colombo because it is near the main international shipping route across the Indian Ocean.

The modernisation of Galle, under the consortium's build, operate and transfer project, could help ease pressure on Colombo port and allow big container ships to save eight hours by not deviating to Colombo.
Trans-shipment occurs when a vessel discharges cargo at an intermediate port and the goods are unloaded to another ship bound for the final destination.
